newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks hold gains, end up on FOMC meeting.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks hold gains, end up on FOMC meeting.

text.p: Mexican stocks retained midsession gains to close up on Wednesday after the Federal Open Market Committee decided not to change U.S. interest rates, analysts and traders said.

"The FOMC decision came as no surprise and had been discounted by the market, but it did at least dispel some uncertainty on the international front," said Esteban Rojas, deputy research director at the Arka brokerage.
The blue chip IPC index closed up 26.54 points, or 0.79 percent, at 3,400.96. Volume was improved over recent sessions at 108.2 million shares traded.
On the broad market, 110 stocks were traded, of which gainers outnumbered losers by 45 to 33.
Cement firm Cemex and phone company Telmex were notable gainers, with their CPO and L series shares up ten and 95 centavos, respectively, at 28.40 and 12.60 pesos.

"Companies that weigh heavily in the IPC, like Cemex and Telmex, have been reaching record prices. Cemex was cheap and dealers, especially foreigners, had hit it very hard because of its debt. But it's a good company," said a floor trader.
A notable loser was publishing stock Gfesa, down 11 centavos to 2.09 pesos.
Gfesa announced it had signed a letter of intent with Bankers Trust to search for a minority partner.
"The market reacted a little oddly to the GFesa announcement, but it is an easy stock to manipulate," said a dealer.
Technical analysts noted that the IPC closed at a psychological barrier.

"We could see profit-taking between 3,400 and 3,450 points, which would help the rally to continue. Good Q3 GDP data MXAAP could help," Rojas added. Mexico's third quarter gross domestic product figures are due November 26.
"The only cause for concern is the Dow. If it adjusts sharply downwards, it will hurt us. If it continues to move sideways, we see no problems," Rojas said.
The Dow Jones ended up 8.20 points, or 0.13 percent, at a closing record of 6,274.24.
